cards.title: Top of the Ladder
cards.instruction: Carry yourself as the highest-status person present. Treat questions as requests for your approval.

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll decide how we handle this. Your plate's back in the cupboard, ready for Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That one's got flowers. Ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can question the details after my decision. I'll take that one. The potatoes will cover the flowers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not hiding it under potatoes. I want six matching plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get five more before lunch. Keep the plain ones for spares; there's no need to count those today.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 decides and A5 commands spare storage, but A3 stock question delay does not specify approval over inspection or the replacement plan.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 pattern mismatch causes A3 potato cover; B4 matching-set demand causes A5 five more plates and no counting, after an irrelevant restriction.

relationship.evidence: B2 recognizes the wrong pattern and B4 refuses concealment, plausibly wanting a coherent lunch setting.

heightening.evidence: B4 rejects a single concealed substitute, so A5 expands replacement to the whole visible set while discouraging inventory.

specificity.evidence: A1 returned plate and B2 plain-versus-floral mismatch establish the restoration problem without needing the original accident.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 no-need-to-count hint is earned by the missing match, though A3 stock preface is clumsy.
